walkthroughs.body_html:
Economic Objectives and the Role of Government — a core area of GCSE Economics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Economic Objectives and the Role of Government brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Economic Objectives and the Role of Government.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Changes to interest rates in the UK are decided by:
options: HM Treasury
MPC of the Bank of England
Office for National Statistics
Prime Minister

mcqs.q: Which is a fiscal policy tool?
options: Interest rates
Income tax
Money supply
Exchange rates

mcqs.q: How is economic growth shown on a Production Possibility Curve?
options: Opportunity cost is the money price of something.
Growth is shown by moving from inside the curve to a point on the curve.
By an outward shift of the entire curve — reflecting an increase in productive capacity through more or better resources, technology, or skills.
Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a shift in demand and a movement along the demand curve?
options: Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.
A change in price shifts the demand curve.
Demand always falls when supply increases.
A movement along the curve is caused by a change in price; a shift of the whole curve is caused by changes in other factors (income, tastes, substitute prices).
Demand always falls when supply increases.
The value of the next-best alternative foregone when a choice is made — the real cost of a decision in terms of what you give up.
Opportunity cost is the total of everything you give up when making a choice.
Opportunity cost is the money price of something.
